A co-educational day and boarding school from Early Years to Sixth Form
Founded in 1842, we are a school that believes that academic success is driven by outstanding pastoral care and a well-rounded education. Our open and calm environment gives students the confidence and mindset to work to their full potential.
Start your journey
As a team, we place great value on human experience, collaboration and connection, so encourage you to come and experience Sibford for yourself.
Values driven
Our Quaker roots inspire and inform our attitude and approach. We live and learn by our core values of endeavour, respect, community and kindness, and each shapes our unique culture as well as the young adults our students become.
Nurturing Every Individual
Pastoral care is at the heart of everything we do — nurturing emotional wellbeing, mutual respect, and a strong sense of belonging. Through our Quaker values and dedicated support, we guide each student to grow with confidence, compassion, and resilience.
Broad curriculum
A vibrant and varied curriculum enriched by a wealth of co-curricular activities encourages individuals to discover and follow their own path, whether it’s a traditional academic one, creative arts, technology or horticulture.
Meet your extended family
Boarders join us from Year 7 onwards as either a full, weekly or flexi-boarder. Our two houses offer a friendly, family-style environment.

pageCache.pageTitle: Individual Success at the Heart of Sibford's Best-Ever GCSE Results - Sibford
pageCache.text:
Individual Success at the Heart of Sibford’s Best-Ever GCSE Results
Students at Sibford School are celebrating the strongest GCSE results in the school’s history, with record academic outcomes alongside some exceptional individual achievements.
Three quarters of Sibford pupils achieved grades 7–9 within their results and at the very highest level, pupils across the year group are celebrating multiple Grade 9s, with some exceptional individual performances.
There were also outstanding performances across individual departments. Every GCSE grade awarded in Music and Design Technology was at grades 7–9, while 83% of Higher Spanish grades and 57% of Higher Mathematics grades were also at this level.
Head Rebecca Evans said that while the record results demonstrate the academic ambition of the school, the individual stories behind them remain the most important measure of success.
“We are enormously proud that these are the strongest GCSE results in Sibford’s history. Three quarters of our pupils have the highest grades represented within their results, with pupils across the year group celebrating multiple Grade 9s. It demonstrates very clearly that young people achieve at the very highest academic level at Sibford.
“But what matters most to us is the individual behind every result. At Sibford, academic ambition has never meant expecting every young person to achieve the same thing. It means having the highest possible ambition for each individual.
“For one pupil, an extraordinary achievement might be multiple Grade 9s. For another, it might be securing a result that once seemed beyond their reach. The numbers cannot tell those stories, but as a school we know what sits behind every one of them.”
The results reflect strong performances across the breadth of Sibford’s curriculum, from mathematics, sciences and languages to humanities, technology and the creative arts.
Rebecca Evans added:
“Being an inclusive school and being academically ambitious are not competing ideas. In fact, we believe one strengthens the other. When young people are known, supported and challenged as individuals, they can achieve remarkable things.
“These may be the best GCSE results in Sibford’s history, but today isn’t really about records. It is about the young people, their individual journeys and what these results enable them to do next.
“We are incredibly proud of every one of them and look forward to seeing them continue to Shape Their Story.”
Sibford holds regular open events throughout the year and welcomes personal visits. The next whole school open events take place on Friday 18 September and Thursday 15 October. To book a place, visit click here or call 01295 781 203.

Creative Artsat Sibford
Our Values in Action:
Creativity is woven into the fabric of life at Sibford.
Whether painting in our light-filled studios, performing under stage lights, or composing in a soundproof practice room, students are given the freedom and encouragement to explore, express, and create.
We believe the arts are more than subjects—they’re a powerful way for young people to find their voice, build confidence, and see the world through different lenses. From the youngest children to Sixth Formers, every pupil has the opportunity to shine in their own unique way.
Drama
Our drama studio and performance hall, complete with full lighting rig and raked seating, provide inspiring spaces for students to explore performance, production, and stagecraft. This summer sees the building of our exciting outdoor community theatre. Drama at Sibford is an invitation to step into someone else’s shoes—and to grow while doing it. Classes learn the value of working as an ensemble.
Each year, our school production brings the whole community together—on stage, behind the scenes, and in the audience. Recent productions such as Les Misérables, Cabaret, and Macbeth, at Broughton castle, have seen students take centre stage as performers, set designers, costume makers, and technical crew. Everyone plays a part, and every part is valued.
Sibford is proud to offer extra-curricular LAMDA lessons, available individually or in pairs from Year 3 – 13. These sessions help develop confidence, vocal and physical communication skills and creativity in students.
Music
Our Music School offers first-class facilities, from practice rooms to recording and technical studios. Whether rehearsing in a band, orchestra, or solo performance, students of all levels find a place to grow and perform. There are numerous performing opportunities from the ‘Sound of Sibford’ at the Mill Arts Centre Banbury, Christmas Concerts, instrumental showcases, music meetings or competing in music festivals.
From Early Years through to Sixth Form, pupils are encouraged to learn instruments, join ensembles, and take part in concerts and performances. With brass, woodwind, strings, percussion, piano, and guitar on offer, musical expression is open to all—whether you’re picking up an instrument for the first time or preparing for a Grade 8 exam.
Art & Design
Our purpose-built Art School is a vibrant hub of creativity, housing studios for painting, textiles, ceramics, and sculpture. Whether experimenting with colour or shaping clay, pupils are encouraged to explore a range of materials and techniques. Work is regularly celebrated in our on-site gallery, giving students the experience of exhibiting in a professional space.
In Design & Technology, ideas are brought to life through a fully equipped suite that supports work in wood, metal, and plastics. Our Food and Nutrition facilities also inspire creativity—with eight self-contained kitchens and a live demonstration space, pupils learn the art of cooking in a space that mirrors a professional environment.
Shape your story
We believe that the best way to experience the unique atmosphere of Sibford is to visit us in person. We warmly invite you to attend one of our Open events or arrange a personal tour to see our vibrant community in action.​

InspectionReport
Information for Families:
Latest Report
Sibford School was inspected by ISI in October 2024.
“The school’s ethos of welcome and inclusion permeates every aspect of school life. There is a palpable sense of kindness, in interactions between pupils and modelled by their teachers, Pupils model the school’s ethos and aims of collective stillness and reflection in assemblies, lessons and during social times. As a result, pupils behave well.”
“Leaders work collaboratively and adeptly together to provide an academic and pastoral education reflecting the ethos of the school. This ethos is based on the school’s values of endeavour, respect, community and kindness. Leaders take into account the needs of the pupils and the views of parents to prioritise the most important things that they need to do.”
“Pupils, including boarders, feel safe and are confident that there is a trusted adult they can speak to, if they have any concerns.”

Pastoral Care
Our Values in Action:
At Sibford, we believe that education extends beyond academic achievement.
Rooted in our Quaker values of kindness, respect, community, and endeavour, we are committed to nurturing the whole individual. Our approach fosters not only intellectual growth but also emotional well-being, social responsibility, and a lifelong love of learning.​ A distinctive feature of our culture is the use of first name and surname between pupils and staff, fostering a sense of equality and mutual respect.
Our pastoral care is central to this ethos. We provide a supportive environment where students are encouraged to understand themselves, build meaningful relationships, and engage with the world around them as compassionate and confident individuals. Our dedicated staff are always available to listen and respond to student concerns, ensuring that any challenges are addressed promptly and empathetically.​
Our approach to discipline mirrors our values—focusing on reflection, restoration, and learning from mistakes — helping students take responsibility and grow from their experiences.
To support our students’ well-being, we offer a comprehensive range of services, including an on-campus health centre staffed by a registered nurse, access to an on-campus counselling services, and an independent listener. These resources are integral to our commitment to each student’s personal development and happiness.​
We also value and actively promote student voice. By encouraging students to express their ideas and participate in decision-making processes, we foster a sense of ownership and belonging within our community. This inclusive approach helps students develop into socially responsible individuals who are prepared to make positive contributions to society.​
At Sibford, we celebrate each student’s unique talents and perspectives, guiding them to become the very best they can be. Our holistic approach to education ensures that students leave us not only with strong academic foundations but also with the confidence, resilience, and compassion to navigate life beyond school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Sibford Celebrates Strong Academic Results and Individual Success - Sibford
pageCache.text:
Sibford Celebrates Strong Academic Results and Individual Success
Students at Sibford School are celebrating strong A Level and Level 3 results, with almost 60% of the year group achieving at least one A* or A grade (or equivalent), alongside excellent outcomes across a broad range of subjects.
As a proudly inclusive school, Sibford has always focused on the progress, achievement and ambitions of each individual. This year’s results demonstrate that this commitment sits firmly alongside high academic outcomes.
There was particular cause for celebration across a breadth of subject areas. 100% of grades in Textiles and Economics were at A*/A and 100% of grades in Religious Studies and Fine Art were at A*–B. Alongside this 67% of grades in Further Mathematics, Sociology and Product Design were at A*–B, while 60% of Mathematics grades were at A*–B, including 40% at A*/A.
Head Rebecca Evans said:
“We are immensely proud of this year group. Sibford is an inclusive school with high academic expectations, and these results demonstrate that those two things go hand in hand. Almost 60% of our students achieving at least one A or A* grade, or equivalent, is something worth celebrating, particularly alongside the breadth of strong subject results. But Results Day at Sibford will always be about individuals rather than simply percentages. Behind every grade is a young person with their own strengths and ambitions. For some, success means achieving the very highest grades; for others, it means exceeding expectations, overcoming barriers or securing the result they need for their chosen next step.
That individuality is reflected in the destinations of the Class of 2026. Students are progressing to universities across the country to study subjects including Medicine, Data Science, Biomedical Sciences, Economics, History, Sociology, Computer Science, Engineering, Artisan Food Production and the creative arts.
Destinations include Russell Group universities such as Exeter, Leeds, Nottingham and Sheffield, alongside specialist and modern universities selected for the strength of particular courses. Other students are taking different routes into their futures through apprenticeships, employment and further training.
Rebecca Evans added:
“There should never be a single definition of success at 18. Whether a young person is heading to university, beginning an apprenticeship, entering employment or pursuing a creative or technical ambition, what matters is that they leave Sibford ready and excited for their next step.
“I am enormously grateful to our staff and families for the support they have given this year group. Most importantly, congratulations to our students. We are incredibly proud of both what they have achieved and the young adults they have become.”
Sibford School wishes every member of the Class of 2026 the very best for the future.
Sibford holds regular open events throughout the year and welcomes personal visits. The next whole school open events take place on Friday 18 September and Thursday 15 October. To book a place, visit click here or call 01295 781 203.

Classes &Clubs
At Sibford, we believe in community and the joy of shared experiences. Our range of classes and clubs is open to all, offering opportunities to learn, connect, and grow together.
Active camps holiday club
Activity Camps provides a high quality, school holiday multi-activity camp for 4-14-year-olds here at Sibford. Visit oxfordactive.co.uk/active-camps/sibford-school/ to learn more.
Community orchestra
This exciting musical adventure open to all instrumentalist from Sibford School and the surrounding area.It is a wonderful opportunity for instrumentalists to experience playing in an orchestra, explore a variety of musical styles, develop new skills and enjoy live music making.
Rehearsals take place on a Sunday once a month in the Main Hall from 2.30pm – 4.30pm. Tea and cake are also on the itinerary.
If you require further information about the Sibford Community Orchestra, please contact Fiona Hudson [email protected].
Pottery classes
Pottery classes course runs on Tuesday and Wednesday evenings and includes hand-building techniques, slab building, throwing on the wheel and decorating with coloured slips.
For further information or to sign up email [email protected].
Swimming pool and lessons
Click here to learn more about the public swim sessions and swimming lessons in our 25m swimming pool. (link to swimming pool page)
Waterbabies
Swimming lessons for babies and toddlers are held at Sibford School on Wednesdays and Fridays.For more information, visit the Waterbabies website.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to Sibford Senior School - Sibford
pageCache.text:
Sibford
Ages 11 – 16
Where your child grows in confidence
Space to discover
At Sibford, we have always believed that a nurturing approach and a focus on holistic education create the best environment for pupils to thrive.
Empowering pupils to develop a life-long thirst for learning sits at the heart of our approach. We encourage them to broaden their horizons, explore their curiosity, and think independently. Our aim is to instil the belief that each of us has something meaningful to offer, so we encourage them to cherish their uniqueness, to actively seek out and nurture their talents, helping them build the confidence they need for 21st-century challenges.
Our broad and balanced curriculum reflects our belief in the power of a well-rounded education all disciplines are given equal respect. While some pupils shine in mathematics, science, or history, others flourish in the arts, horticulture, or sport. We are here for all of them. Our outstanding GCSE results are a testament to the effectiveness of our holistic approach.
Space to grow
Nurturing at Sibford doesn’t just mean care—it also means providing the right level of challenge so pupils can truly grow.
Pupils benefit from small class sizes where dedicated teachers nurture, inspire, and stretch them, encouraging them to discover and harness their own talents. Staff build strong, supportive relationships with pupils, offering a foundation of mutual trust and encouragement.
We know our pupils, identifying and meeting the needs of our most able through enrichment and extension activities, while also providing specialist support for those who need it.
Key Stage 3 (Years 7–9)
Pupils study a wide range of subjects designed to help them discover and develop their individual talents and passions.
Key Stage 4 (Years 10–11)
Our core curriculum includes English, Mathematics, Science, and Physical Education, with GCSE option choices made in Year 9. Across every subject, we encourage independent thinking and a resilient approach to learning.
Our varied curriculum is enriched by visiting speakers, external school trips, and extensive use of our staffed library and ICT facilities. All pupils take part in our physical education programme, promoting health and development while enjoying our excellent sporting facilities, including our swimming pool, outdoor theatre and climbing wall.
Space to belong
Life at Sibford is rich with opportunity.
Pupils are encouraged to get involved in a wide variety of co-curricular activities, from sport and music to creative clubs and community initiatives. These experiences play a vital role in building confidence, fostering friendships, and developing a strong sense of social responsibility.
We are committed to providing an education that not only focuses on academic excellence but also fosters holistic development, preparing our pupils to take their place in the world with confidence and compassion.

We believe that the best way to experience the unique atmosphere of Sibford is to visit us in person. We warmly invite you to attend one of our Open events or arrange a personal tour to see our vibrant community in action.​

Intensive English
For: students needing to strengthen their English before joining Year 10 (pre-GCSE) or Sixth Form (pre-A Level).
This is an opportunity for them to enhance their grammar and vocabulary while developing essential reading, writing, speaking, and listening skills for studying and living here in the UK.
Details
Pre-Intermediate (B1 CEFR):
Headway Pre-Intermediate Course
Intermediate (B2 CEFR):
Headway Intermediate Course
Maths, with possible GCSE entry depending on ability. Art, Media, Food, Design Technology, Sport, Music, Business Studies, English Culture Through Books and Film.
GCSEs, A Levels or BTECS, IELTS or Foundation Courses.
Mainstream with EAL
For: students ready to follow the British curriculum who want to develop language skills.
An opportunity for students to expand their vocabulary and grammar understanding by taking part in activities focused on communication.
Students will improve their English by a level each academic year, working on building vocabulary and grammar, listening and speaking through communication activities and the ability to write in a range of styles.
In Year 11, they can take the IGCSE in English as a Second Language.
Details
GCSES with IGCSE in ESL or Sixth Form with A Levels/BTECs and IELTS.
IELTS Preparation
For: Sixth Form students on A Level or BTEC courses.
We equip them with the language skills and techniques needed to achieve strong results in the International English Language Testing System – essential for university applications.
Details

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to Sibford Early Years - Sibford
pageCache.text:
Sibford
Ages 3 – 5
Where your child’s journey begins
Space to discover
We love being outside and getting muddy – a waterproof all-in-one is essential.
The best kind of learning happens in mud pits, where children work together creating rivers, engaging in imaginative play, or discover minibeasts. Our 50-acre grounds provide endless inspiration for learning – from picking blackberries for crumbles to harvesting vegetables for soups we cook together.
Nature walks invite us to explore the changing seasons, go pond dipping, or learn about plants. Our continuous care gives children space to develop their interests.
Large outdoor bricks transform into dens, tractors, or spaceships for journeys through time and imagination.
Children benefit from specialist Forest School teachers, and a chance to dip into a new skill like horticulture, pottery, swimming, magical adventures or music.
Space to grow
We aim to plant the seeds for a deep love of learning that flourishes at Sibford.
We encourage questions, curiosity, and child-led exploration. Our knowledge of each child, combined with small class sizes enables is to truly tailor learning – challenging some and taking a play-based approach for others.
In Reception, we read with children each day. They genuinely enjoy this one-on-one time with us, because we make space for success, with many exceeding year-end reading expectations.
Our curriculum focuses on stewardship and environmental care. We see ourselves as stewards of Sibford’s flora and fauna – building hedgehog houses, planting wildflowers for pollinators, making bird feeders, or rescuing playground worms. Children develop a deep respect for nature and understand the importance of caring for our world.
Space to belong
Early Years feels much like a family.
We focus on the prime areas of early development, knowing that when children feel safe with a sense of belonging, they can build strong relationships, settle happily, and be the best they can be in their learning.
We work closely with parents to make sure children settle well. Helping them explore emotions and navigate feelings is key, so we invest time teaching collaborative play and conflict resolution, building community and cultivating kindness. It’s a joy watching our older children model kind behaviour to guide the younger nursery friends.
Children can join Sibford Nursery from September after turning three, with Reception welcoming four-year-olds. Under the Early Education Funding Scheme, nursery children (ages 3-4) are eligible for up to 15 hours free funding weekly.
Our Day
8.30 – 10.35 Welcome and play
Children are welcomed into the main classroom, where they can play and settle, ready for a day of learning. They will have access to continuous provision both inside and outside during this time. We encourage children to follow their own lines of interest during this time and let them take a lead in their own learning.
Within this morning session, the reception children will be taken out for a short and discrete phonics/English session. The length of these sessions links closely to the age and ability of the child.
At 10.15 all children will go outside to enjoy a play session with KS1.
10.35 – 11.05 Snack and a story
The children come in for a healthy snack of fruit, fresh bread and milk and listen to a story. After this we will have a short maths session. For nursery, they may just take part in a warm up maths song and for reception this may involve more targeted teaching.
11.05 – 11.45 Reading
The children will follow their own lines of interest in the main classroom with one adult while the teacher reads with the reception children 1:1. The reading session is very much tailored to the individual needs of the child and is something the children very much look forward too.
11.45 – 1.30 Lunch
We head over to the Dining Hall where we have our own small room space to eat our lunch. We model good table manners and enjoy conversation. If the children stay for lunch they will receive a hot meal and they are encouraged to try new foods but we will not make a child eat anything. After lunch, the children have the opportunity to play in our Orchard and willow tunnel.
1.30 - 4.00 Afternoon activities
We have a whole array of lovely opportunities available for the children in the afternoons. They have Physical Education, Forest School in our onsite Forest School, Magical Adventures, music, swimming, pottery all taught by specialist teachers as well as activities in class such as cooking, puppet making and welly walks.
4.00 – 5.20 After school care
The school day finishes at 4pm when we then move into aftercare. This takes place in the Early Years setting where the children are given a snack before moving to the main room for a play session. Nursery children can remain until 4.30pm without additional charge. Recpetion children can remain until 5.20pm. (Booking is required)
5.20 – 6.00pm Tea
There is the option to stay for tea. This is paid for and must be booked in advance to ensure we have the necessary staff ratios.

How toFind Us
By Car
Our address is Sibford School, Sibford Ferris, Banbury, Oxfordshire. OX15 5QL
By Rail
Banbury Railway station is under 1 hour away from London (Marylebone or Paddington) and 15 minutes away from Oxford.
Taxis are available at Banbury station and the journey to Sibford School takes about 15 minutes.
By Air
Sibford is just 55 minutes by road from Birmingham International Airport and 90 minutes from Heathrow Airport.

Hiring facilities &lettings
Sibford has a number of facilities that benefit the local community and are available for hire.
Outdoor Pitches
In our 50-acre grounds, there are pitches for rugby, football, hockey and cricket as well as netball and tennis courts.
Sports Hall
Our versatile sports hall provides an excellent indoor space for a wide range of activities, including badminton, netball, five-a-side football and indoor cricket nets. Whether for training, matches or recreational use, the hall offers a flexible, high-quality venue suitable for clubs, schools and community groups.
Swimming Pool
Sibford’s 25m indoor heated swimming pool is available to hire at various time across the week.
Climbing Wall
A large, full-height climbing wall spanning 3 walls, perfect for beginners and intermediates.
Lettings
Sibford welcomes bookings over school holiday periods, when our two residential boarding houses and other facilities are available for hire. We can also offer catering services where needed.
Our two boarding houses offer lounges, kitchens and accommodation comprising single, twin and dorm-style rooms accommodating a maximum of 70 people.

Quaker Meetings,Reflection & Stillness
Our Values in Action:
At Sibford, Meeting for Worship is at the heart of our school life—a time when we come together in shared stillness to reflect, listen, and simply be.
Rooted in our Quaker heritage, these Meetings are a calm and inclusive space for students and staff to pause amidst the busyness of school life.
Held several times each week, our meetings begin and end in silence.
Within this quiet, anyone—student or staff—may feel moved to speak.
This practice nurtures a deep sense of community. It encourages us to listen—not just to others, but to ourselves—and to appreciate the value of quiet reflection.For many, the experience of Meeting for Worship stays with them long after their time at Sibford. In a world that often moves too fast, these moments of shared stillness remind us of the strength found in silence and the connections we build when we take time to pause together.

Scholarships &Bursaries
Scholarships
“A Sibford Scholarship is not just about celebrating excellence, it’s about developing it and sharing it.”
The aims of the scholarship programme at Sibford are:
to encourage students who are exceptionally gifted and talented to join the school.
to recognise outstanding talent within the school at key transition stages.
to continue the school’s long tradition of providing public benefit.
Sibford scholarship students are given the opportunity to engage in a wide range of activities and extra support in their chosen field of talent by staff who are experts in their field and encouraged to challenge themselves to achieve at the very highest level.
Categories of scholarship:
Academic:
where a student shows exceptional academic ability and potential.
Creative Arts:
Performing Arts:
Drama, Music and Musical Theatre.
Sport
In Senior School All-Rounder scholarships may be awarded at the Head‘s discretion to candidates who show promise in more than one area.

Bursaries
Sibford is committed to helping more young people reach their potential and encouraging them to achieve their aspirations whatever these might be. Bursaries are not dependent on particular academic or creative achievement. They are, however, subject to annual testing of parental means and may be varied upwards or downwards depending on parental circumstances.
We offer a limited number of means-tested bursaries for which families of prospective students from both Quaker and non-Quaker families may apply. For current pupils whose families encounter unexpected difficulties, short term emergency bursary support may be available in exceptional circumstances.
Sibford’s bursary funds are very limited therefore competition for bursary funding is always strong and only given in exceptional circumstances; simply meeting our financial criteria for a means-tested bursary does not guarantee an award being made.
An independent company, Bursary Administration Ltd (BAL) will review and assess the application and arrange to visit you. Depending on their assessment of your application, the Bursary Committee may propose an award against day fees only (but not on any extra charges).
Applications for bursary assistance are reviewed annually and we will contact existing bursary holders towards the end of Spring term to request updated information. We will also work with BAL during this review process.
Bursary applications for entry in September 2027 close on 16 October 2026 for Year 7 applicants. A second deadline of 31 January 2027 remains for late applicants and for 2027 applications in other year groups. Families who are interested in applying for a bursary should click to request a bursary information pack below.

Short StayImmersion
We warmly welcome students for short stays ranging from two to four weeks, or up to a full term, throughout the academic year.
These short stays offer students the opportunity to experience the British curriculum whilst also allowing them to immerse themselves in life at Sibford.
Experience the British curriculum and life at Sibford through a shorter stay.
What’s included:
Warm induction to our facilities and community
Integration with British students
Cultural trips and activities with boarders
Comfortable accommodation and meals
Personalised progress report
“Coming to stay at Sibford has been an incredible experience. The studying was fun and we had fantastic outings. Living with people my age from different countries was amazing. Thank you Sibford, I am sad to leave the friends I made here.”
Jacopo, Year 9, Italy

AdmissionsFAQs
We understand that choosing a new school is a significant decision, and with it comes a multitude of questions.
At Sibford, we are committed to providing clarity and support throughout your admissions journey.
Below, you’ll find answers to frequently asked questions about our admissions process.
Should you have any further queries, please don’t hesitate to reach out to our Admissions team. We’re here to help and look forward to welcoming you to the Sibford community.
What does the Sibford day look like?
07:00am – Morning clubs08:00am – Breakfast08:30am – Pupils register in form rooms08:40am – Morning meeting09:00am – Period 109:55am – Period 210:45am – Break11:05am – Period 312:00pm – Period 412:50pm – Lunch13:35pm – Pupils register in form rooms13:40pm – Period 514:35pm – Period 615:30pm – Period 716:20pm – End of lessons / buses depart16:30pm – Snack for boarders and day pupils staying for activities. Prep / activities17:30pm – Boarders break17:45pm – Tea Day pupils may stay for tea provided they have booked 48 hours in advance18:15pm – Boarders prep
How can I visit Sibford?
We hold a Saturday open event in March and open mornings on Fridays throughout the year in September, October, April and June. These give you the chance to see the school in action.
We also hold specific Early Years stay and pay sessions and Junior School and Sixth Form open events throughout the school year.
Click here to sign up to an upcoming open event. Should you wish to have a private tour, please contact 01295 781 2023 or email [email protected].
How do I apply?
Application to Sibford School is through the completion of the appropriate application form and payment of a non-refundable registration fee of £120 inclusive of VAT.
Please click on the relevant entry point below to create an account and apply for Sibford School online:
Early Years application (Nursery and Reception)
Junior School application (Years 1 – 6)
Senior School application (Years 7 – 10)
Sixth Form application (Year 12)
When do I need to apply?
We recommend applying as early as you can for a place at Sibford. Deadlines for applications and varies on which year your child is applying for. Click here to view the deadlines for the coming year.
Where possible we will accommodate in year admissions so please don’t hesitate to contact us.
Where do your networks of minibuses run?
Sibford operates a number of bus routes for pupils to travel to school and back home using both school minibuses and coaches.
Click here to see the current bus routes.
